message.content:
Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) belong to two different orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively—but both are part of the larger clade **Laurasiatheria**.  
Their last common ancestor was a small, early mammal that lived roughly 70 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous, before the lineages that would become modern carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates diverged.
